summary: The psychology and personal-development material treats agency as something shaped by reflective habits, social performances, goals, interfaces, and trusted infrastructures. Journaling, gratitude, connection-making, creator positioning, goal setting, and stochastic-gradient-descent metaphors help people steer attention and motivation, while workplace satire, platform metrics, UX reporting, CLI behavior, and digital maps show how environments can quietly redirect behavior. The strongest qualification is that tools and systems that feel useful or confidence-building can also become status games, opaque interfaces, privacy risks, or brittle abstractions unless evidence, ownership, and trust are made explicit.
